name: Siemens Digital Industries Software

profile.address: 27930, Southwest Parkway Avenue, Wilsonville, Clackamas County, Oregon, 97070
profile.reading:
The building sits within the Wilsonville, Oregon campus that has served as headquarters for the electronic design automation company now known as Siemens EDA since long before that name existed. The campus traces to Mentor Graphics, an Oregon-founded software company that built its headquarters in Wilsonville and grew into one of the three dominant vendors of chip design software worldwide, alongside Synopsys and Cadence. In March 2017 Siemens completed a 4.5 billion dollar acquisition of Mentor Graphics. Under the terms of that deal Mentor kept its Wilsonville headquarters and its workforce intact, continuing to operate as a largely independent subsidiary for several years before Siemens folded the brand into its own naming. From 2017 to 2020 the unit traded as Mentor, a Siemens Business. In January 2021 it was renamed Siemens EDA, now organized under the Siemens Digital Industries Software division.

Facilities tagged HDC on this campus typically refer to internal hosting or data center infrastructure supporting engineering compute, chip simulation, and software licensing operations rather than a leased colocation product sold to outside tenants. Chip design software of the kind Siemens EDA produces depends on very large compute farms for simulation, verification, and regression testing, and a company of this size operating in Wilsonville can be expected to run substantial on-site or co-located infrastructure to support that work, alongside its own product data centers and cloud-hosted EDA tools. None of that internal infrastructure is described in public materials in a way that names this specific building, gives it a square footage, or states an IT load in megawatts. Siemens EDA's public communications concentrate on software products, industry partnerships, and its parent company's broader digital industries strategy, not on facility-level detail for any single building on its Oregon campus.

What can be said with confidence is the continuity of the site itself. Wilsonville has hosted this company's headquarters for decades, through the Mentor Graphics era, the Siemens acquisition, and the subsequent rebrand, without a relocation. That continuity, combined with the scale of compute a modern EDA vendor requires, is what places a facility of this kind on a data center registry even though the operator has not chosen to publish operational specifics for it.

reading: Siemens Digital Industries Software operates its Electronic Design Automation headquarters, which the company describes as its largest Digital Industries Software site worldwide, in the Portland, Oregon metropolitan area. The Oregon operations trace back to Mentor Graphics, a long-established electronic design automation company that Siemens acquired in 2017 and folded into its Digital Industries Software division. The site develops EDA software used to design, simulate, and verify electronic systems including microchips, supporting semiconductor and electronics customers globally, and in 2022 the group became a charter member of the Intel Foundry Services Accelerator EDA Alliance, an industry initiative aimed at building an ecosystem for next-generation chip design and manufacturing. As with several other technology company facilities in this registry, the Oregon site functions primarily as a software engineering and research and development headquarters rather than a wholesale or commercial data center, with internal compute infrastructure existing to support chip design software development, simulation, and testing workloads for Siemens's own product engineering rather than external colocation customers.
